changelog: Inserted a principle to avoid creating very short predicate-only fragments and to prefer keeping verbs, their complements, and scope-bearing operators together — addresses the leftward-cut bias that isolates predicates.

Inserted a principle to strongly penalize cuts whose following fragment has high probability of contradicting or overturning the prior material (contra ≳0.5) — addresses underweighting of high post-cut contradiction.
Paraphrased C1–C8 to shorter, clearer judgments to cut overall prompt length and reduce leftward bias while preserving intent (addresses size overbudget and many critique points).
Strengthened C2 into an explicit prohibition against leaving tiny fragments containing only a predicate/auxiliary/negation without required complements (addresses finding about isolating predicates).

Inserted a new core principle (after C2) that requires marking cuts with high post-cut contradiction (contra ≳ 0.5) as unsafe and lowering their rank substantially (directly addresses finding about underweighting high contra).
Deleted ten largest Examples (E1, E3, E4, E5, E6, E8, E9, E10, E12, E13) to bring the prompt under the size budget and keep the example set within the 8-example limit.
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_738 to teach the scorer about predicate/negation isolation (addresses leftward-cut bias that creates tiny predicate-only fragments).
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_990 to show how separating negation/predicate can invert or mislead meaning in short fragments (reinforces keeping verbs and scope together).
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_845 to demonstrate discourse/connective risks and cases where post-cut material can change the preceding clause's force (addresses underweighting of contra).
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_1116 to illustrate high post-cut contradiction from exceptions/contrast (teaches strong penalties when contra ≳ 0.5).
